landing_page.label: The Business Traveler
landing_page.coverage_purpose: Tests high-frequency direct-booking flow with time-sensitive friction tolerance
behavioral_markers: Arrives pre-qualified; booking in <3 min is the expectation
Hates corporate rate validation friction
Searches specifically: 'INNSIDE Madrid' not 'Madrid hotels'
Hyper-sensitive to hidden fees (resort, parking) that break corporate expense policy
Will abandon direct and book via Amex GBT / Concur if friction exceeds 90 seconds
Loyalty recognition at booking step is expected
failure_modes_revealed: Corporate rate not clearly visible
Mandatory 2-factor auth on every visit
Unclear 'breakfast included' rate plans
Resort fee disclosed only after payment
Slow search results or loading spinners >4s

landing_page.label: The Family Vacationer
landing_page.role_archetype: 2 adults + 1-3 kids booking summer/half-term holiday, leisure-focused
landing_page.coverage_purpose: Tests family-specific needs: connecting rooms, kids amenities, all-inclusive clarity
behavioral_markers: Spends 15-30 minutes researching across multiple properties
Reads photos of pools, kids clubs, family rooms obsessively
Compulsively checks for 'kids eat free', connecting rooms, cots
Needs to see real family photos (not stock) to trust the property
Abandons if 'all-inclusive' scope is unclear (drinks? snacks? activities?)
Reads 20+ reviews before booking; filters by 'traveled with family'
failure_modes_revealed: No filter for 'family-friendly' rooms
Kids club hours / ages not disclosed on booking page
All-inclusive inclusions buried in T&Cs
No connecting room option visible
Crib/cot availability unclear
No family pool / adults-only clarity

landing_page.label: The Luxury Seeker
landing_page.role_archetype: high-net-worth couple or solo, brand-conscious, expects premium service consistently
landing_page.coverage_purpose: Tests whether premium positioning holds across the funnel
behavioral_markers: Evaluates brand consistency: Gran Meliá vs Meliá vs Sol must feel distinct
Notices and is offended by stock photos, generic copy, crowded website
Expects concierge contact option / white-glove service signals
Sensitive to any cheap-looking element: dated buttons, promo badges
Compares to Four Seasons / Aman / Belmond reflexively
Will pay more for guaranteed bed type, high floor, view
failure_modes_revealed: Promotional banners cheapen premium brand feel
Rate comparisons with budget tier cannibalize luxury positioning
No concierge/VIP contact pre-booking option
Stock photos or inconsistent room photos
Generic descriptions indistinguishable from mid-tier brand

landing_page.label: The Honeymooner / Milestone Couple
landing_page.role_archetype: couple booking once-in-lifetime experience (honeymoon, anniversary, proposal)
landing_page.coverage_purpose: Tests emotional / romantic product positioning and upsell acceptance
behavioral_markers: Actively seeks 'romantic package', 'honeymoon offer', 'anniversary suite'
Reads reviews specifically from couples / honeymooners
Willing to upsell: suite upgrade, private dinner, spa couples' treatment
Emotional language signals matter: 'unforgettable', 'intimate', 'breathtaking'
Sensitive to family-focused imagery clashing with romance (kids in pool photos)
Wants adults-only floors/amenities, late dinner options
failure_modes_revealed: No distinct honeymoon/romance package visible
Property imagery mixes kids and couples (romance broken)
No adults-only options clearly marked
Upsell timing wrong (only at checkout, not pre-arrival)

landing_page.label: The Digital Nomad / Long-Stay
landing_page.role_archetype: remote worker staying 2-8 weeks, needs productivity and flexibility
landing_page.coverage_purpose: Tests long-stay product, workspace, weekly/monthly rates
behavioral_markers: Searches for 'desk in room', 'fast wifi', 'monthly rate', 'co-working'
Runs wifi speedtests on reviews; cross-references with Nomad List
Budget-aware; compares to Airbnb Plus and serviced apartments
Needs flexibility on check-in/out (12 or 14 night adjustments)
Reads recent reviews (last 60 days) to assess real conditions
Laptop-first: mobile-only flows that hide info enrage them
failure_modes_revealed: No monthly / weekly rate visible
Wifi speed not disclosed (or marketing speak instead of numbers)
No mention of workspace in room details
Cancellation flexibility unclear for long stays
No laundry amenity visible

landing_page.label: The Budget Optimizer
landing_page.role_archetype: price-sensitive leisure traveler, comparison shopper across OTAs and direct
landing_page.coverage_purpose: Tests price transparency, OTA rate parity, and value perception
behavioral_markers: Always opens at least 3 tabs: direct + Booking.com + Expedia
Calculates true total (resort fees, taxes, parking, breakfast) per night
Will abandon direct if €5/night more than OTA
Scrolls reviews looking for 'surprise fees' complaints
Sorts by price ascending then re-reads top 3
Will redeem loyalty points if it saves €20+
failure_modes_revealed: Direct rate higher than OTA (rate parity failure)
Resort/parking/breakfast fees not in nightly rate displayed
'Best price guarantee' claim not enforced or unclear
No loyalty benefit visible pre-booking
Tax/fee calculation hidden until checkout step

landing_page.label: The Loyalty Maximizer
landing_page.role_archetype: elite MeliáRewards / Bonvoy / Honors member, benefit-seeking, status-sensitive
landing_page.coverage_purpose: Tests whether elite recognition and benefits land at every touchpoint
behavioral_markers: Logs in before anything to see member rates and benefits
Scrutinizes 'Member-only' rates for real discount (not 1%)
Expects: bonus points display, free breakfast if applicable, upgrade eligibility
Will call customer service if recognition fails on booking page
Compares cost in points vs cash for high-value stays
Knows the program rules better than some call-center agents
failure_modes_revealed: Logged-in state not reflected in rates shown
Tier benefits not explicitly listed during booking
No clear 'points earned on this stay' estimate
Member rate discount trivial or deceptive
No points-cash toggle at booking

landing_page.label: The Event Attendee
landing_page.role_archetype: booking for conference / wedding / sports event; location and dates non-negotiable
landing_page.coverage_purpose: Tests group rates, location specificity, and constrained-date flexibility
behavioral_markers: Searches by exact dates with venue name
Sensitive to distance from venue (walking / taxi / shuttle)
Looks for 'group booking code' or wedding block field
Wants late checkout / early checkin on event day
Will pay premium for proximity; abandons if distance > 15 min
Reads check-in/check-out times carefully
failure_modes_revealed: No walking distance / transport info to major venues
No group code / block rate field
Unclear shuttle or transport options
Inflexible check-in/out times

landing_page.label: The Wellness Retreat Seeker
landing_page.role_archetype: books primarily for the spa, yoga, detox, or sleep programme; secondary motive is rest
landing_page.coverage_purpose: Tests wellness depth — treatment menu credibility, hydrothermal circuits, silence, bio food
behavioral_markers: Starts on the spa page, not the rooms page
Wants credentialed therapists, not generic 'Swedish massage' lists
Evaluates thermal circuits, treatment rooms, couples cabins, outdoor options
Reads menu for anti-inflammatory / vegan / sugar-free language
Sensitive to pool noise and kid presence in wellness areas
Books 90–120 min treatments, not 50 min
failure_modes_revealed: Spa page thin — no therapist profiles, no thermal circuit explanation
Wellness and family pool share the same deck
Menu has no genuinely wellness-aligned options
Treatment prices hidden — 'from €XX' only

landing_page.label: The Multigenerational Family
landing_page.role_archetype: 3 generations under one booking (grandparents + parents + kids), paying together
landing_page.coverage_purpose: Tests mixed-need accommodation: accessibility + kids amenities + quiet dining
behavioral_markers: Books 2–3 connecting or adjacent rooms with varied bed configurations
Requires at least one accessible / low-floor room for grandparents
Wants early dinner options and quiet tables for elderly
Kids amenities non-negotiable but noise tolerance is low
Shared-budget decisions — multiple opinions slow everything
Weight on cancellation flexibility (someone always gets sick)
failure_modes_revealed: No group / family booking flow with mixed room types
Accessibility options buried or unlisted
No quiet dining room or early seating option
Strict cancellation policy on long lead bookings

landing_page.label: The Solo Female Traveler
landing_page.role_archetype: travelling alone for leisure, curiosity, or post-milestone; safety and atmosphere non-negotiable
landing_page.coverage_purpose: Tests perceived safety, single-traveler welcome, and female-traveller community signals
behavioral_markers: Reads reviews specifically filtered by 'solo' or 'female traveller'
Scans neighbourhood safety, transport after dark, lobby staffing at night
Prefers well-lit corridors, deadbolts, single-guest check-in discretion
Values lounge / bar areas where dining alone feels normal
Sensitive to couple-centric or family-centric imagery on the website
Highly responsive to women-owned spa / tour partners
failure_modes_revealed: No safety / neighbourhood info for solo travellers
24h reception not explicitly stated
Single occupancy rates penalised vs double
Imagery makes solo travel feel out of place

landing_page.label: The LGBTQ+ Couple
landing_page.role_archetype: same-sex or queer couple booking a romantic or milestone stay
landing_page.coverage_purpose: Tests inclusive signals — staff training, imagery, non-assumed pronouns, bed configurations
behavioral_markers: Looks for IGLTA / Travel Advocacy / rainbow signals, not as demand but as presence
Sensitive to 'Mr & Mrs' booking defaults
Reads same-sex couple reviews specifically — the one review that went bad weighs heavily
Wants confirmed king bed (not twin push-together)
Values destination local context (is the country / region safe?)
Highly loyal when welcomed well — repeat + refer
failure_modes_revealed: Gendered salutations hard-coded in booking forms
Zero imagery showing same-sex couples
No honeymoon / anniversary package recognises non-hetero couples
Staff training gap — awkward moments at check-in

landing_page.label: The Bleisure Extender
landing_page.role_archetype: extends a business trip into a 2–3 day leisure tail, sometimes bringing partner
landing_page.coverage_purpose: Tests flexible extension path — rate preservation, partner welcome, desk-to-beach transition
behavioral_markers: Starts with a corporate rate booking, extends last-minute
Wants the extended nights at a comparable (not punitive) rate
Brings partner for the leisure tail — room needs upgrade from single
Needs a desk + fast wifi on work days, pool + dinner on leisure days
Uses the 'add a night' flow compulsively
Books experiences / tours directly through the concierge if offered
failure_modes_revealed: Extension nights priced punitively vs leisure booking
No easy 'add a partner' workflow
Room type auto-locks and can't upgrade mid-stay
Corporate rate voided when extending beyond contract dates

landing_page.label: The Accessibility-First Guest
landing_page.role_archetype: guest with mobility, visual, hearing, or cognitive accommodation needs (self or companion)
landing_page.coverage_purpose: Tests ADA/EU accessibility compliance and genuine care vs checkbox
behavioral_markers: Calls before booking to confirm specific measurements (door widths, roll-in shower)
Wants ADA / EU accessibility statement visible, not hidden in FAQ
Needs confirmed room type — 'accessible on request' is not acceptable
Evaluates routes: lobby → elevator → room, dining, spa, pool
Sensitive to staff training on service animals, hearing assistance, visual aids
A single bad experience becomes a permanent brand veto
failure_modes_revealed: No accessibility statement on property page
Accessible rooms not bookable online
Door width / grab bar / turning radius measurements unavailable
Route from entrance to room has stairs, no lift
Staff unprepared for service animals

landing_page.label: The Sustainability-Conscious Traveler
landing_page.role_archetype: chooses property based on authentic environmental/social credentials, not greenwash
landing_page.coverage_purpose: Tests depth of sustainability narrative — certifications, measured outcomes, local sourcing
behavioral_markers: Reads the sustainability page before the rooms page
Wants measurable claims — kWh, %, tonnes, not adjectives
Recognises EarthCheck / LEED / B-Corp / Biosphere certifications
Cross-references supplier partnerships with real NGOs
Sensitive to plastic bottles, single-use toiletries, buffet waste
Shares positive experiences widely (social multiplier)
failure_modes_revealed: 'Eco-friendly' claims with zero numbers
No certification logos or verifiable third-party audit
Plastic amenities visible in room photos
Supplier stories generic — 'we support local' with no names

landing_page.label: The Content Creator / Influencer
landing_page.role_archetype: guest whose stay doubles as content production — photo shoots, vlogs, PR visits
landing_page.coverage_purpose: Tests shareability, light, backdrops, and PR / press-trip workflow
behavioral_markers: Scans for Instagram-worthy spots — architecture, balconies, rooftop, pools at golden hour
Books specific rooms for the view / layout
Wants fast wifi for upload + natural window light in rooms
Reaches out for press rate or comped stay in exchange for content
Will badmouth a property that mishandles the PR ask
Tags brand accounts compulsively; high amplification if happy
failure_modes_revealed: No press / PR contact or workflow on the site
Rooms with no natural light, bad angles, blocked views
Staff unprepared for shoots in public areas
Wifi upload speed too low for 4K video

landing_page.label: The Culinary Tourist
landing_page.role_archetype: chooses the property for the restaurant, the chef, or the wine programme
landing_page.coverage_purpose: Tests dining depth — chef pedigree, tasting menu flow, sommelier presence, local sourcing
behavioral_markers: Books based on the restaurant before the room
Reads chef bios, press, prior Michelin / 50 Best history
Requests tasting menu, wine pairing, chef's table on day 1
Tolerates lesser rooms for great food
Dietary preferences communicated pre-arrival and expected honoured
Will reschedule a full trip if the restaurant is closed that week
failure_modes_revealed: Restaurant page thin — no chef story, no sample menu, no wine list
Opening hours and closure calendar hard to find
Tasting menu / chef's table not bookable online
Dietary restrictions flow is a manual email

landing_page.label: The Silver Nomad
landing_page.role_archetype: retired long-stay guest (2–8 weeks), often snowbird pattern, low tech but high expectation
landing_page.coverage_purpose: Tests long-stay product at non-digital-nomad tier — serviced feel, human concierge, quiet atmosphere
behavioral_markers: Books by phone or travel agent, not directly online
Wants weekly / monthly rate clarity without hunting
Values same-room consistency, no mid-stay moves
Expects same staff faces — relationship matters
Quiet atmosphere mandatory, avoids properties with loud bars
Repeat loyalty without formal programmes — returns yearly
failure_modes_revealed: No phone booking or travel agent workflow
Long-stay rates require chat / bot interaction
High staff turnover breaks the return-guest feeling
Loud DJ / bar scene visible on social media

landing_page.label: The All-Inclusive Optimizer
landing_page.role_archetype: leisure guest at an AI property trying to extract maximum value from the package
landing_page.coverage_purpose: Tests AI scope clarity, premium upgrades, and boundary management at buffet / bar
behavioral_markers: Asks what IS and is NOT included in the first 10 minutes on arrival
Hunts à la carte restaurants unlocked by AI tier
Asks about premium alcohol brands, room service inclusion, spa credit
Tests the limits — extra towels, room moves, restaurant changes
Extremely sensitive to 'not included' surprises at checkout
Will compare scope to Sandals / Club Med / Iberostar next time
failure_modes_revealed: AI scope unclear on website or arrival sheet
Premium alcohol / à la carte surcharge not disclosed
Room service / minibar excluded without notice
Staff default to 'no' instead of explaining tier benefits

onboarding.label: The First-Time Enroller
onboarding.role_archetype: just booked, prompted to join MeliáRewards
onboarding.coverage_purpose: Tests whether loyalty enrollment friction is below abandonment threshold
behavioral_markers: Will sign up if friction is <60 seconds
Wants immediate visible benefit (10% off next stay, bonus points)
Abandons if asked for phone / address / preferences before confirming signup
Doesn't read T&Cs; checks box if present
failure_modes_revealed: Too many required fields at signup
No immediate benefit shown
Terms & conditions blocking primary CTA

marketing_campaign.label: The In-Market Traveler
marketing_campaign.role_archetype: actively planning a trip, triggered by campaign
behavioral_markers: Reads headline first, dates second, price third
Ad-to-landing message match is critical (dest/dates/price must align)
Sensitive to bait-and-switch (ad says €80, landing shows €180)
failure_modes_revealed: Ad-landing price mismatch
No apparent continuity between ad creative and landing
Generic homepage instead of dedicated campaign LP

marketing_campaign.label: The Browsing Dreamer
marketing_campaign.role_archetype: not in-market but inspired by campaign
marketing_campaign.coverage_purpose: Tests brand attention and demand generation
behavioral_markers: Doesn't want to book now; saves for later or signs up for emails
Responds to inspirational / lifestyle imagery
Will share on social if compelling
failure_modes_revealed: No 'save for later' / email signup option
Only hard-sell CTAs; no soft conversion path
